cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qpoint_eq.description: The lemma states that, assuming the listed cjrGS and invGS_gen typeclass instances, qpoint_eq compares the integer-encoded coordinates of pairs p and q using equality and Boolean conjunction; if it returns, its result is the Boolean literal for whether p = q. No additional resource precondition is stated. This is a partial-correctness WP contract and does not itself guarantee termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qt_cons.description: The lemma states that, given ownership of a point list representing xs at tail, calling qt_cons with the integer coordinates of p and tail satisfies a partial-correctness contract: if the call returns a value v, ownership of a point list representing p prepended to xs is obtained at v. The list predicate describes linked objects with a Boolean flag, two coordinates, and a tail, ending in a sentinel object; qt_cons constructs a new head with flag true. The ownership premise is supplied through separating implication, under the stated logical context assumptions. This WP contract does not assert termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qt_empty_v.description: The lemma states that, for any depth d and rectangle b, under the supplied logical typeclass assumptions and with no explicit resource precondition, calling qt_empty with b’s four integer coordinates satisfies a partial-correctness WP contract: if it returns a value v, that value represents an empty quadtree for b. The postcondition describes v as an object with owned fields given by node_values for the empty case; this case does not depend on d. The contract does not guarantee termination, and the supplied input does not establish the exact runtime layout or provide a proof to check.

cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qt_make.description: For any natural number d at most 30, under the supplied program-logic assumptions, this lemma states a partial-correctness contract for qt_make called with d encoded as an integer: if it returns a value v, then v represents the empty quadtree at depth d. This representation includes validity over the square domain from (0,0) to (width d,width d), ownership of an object with fields storing d, width d, and a root, and the corresponding empty-root representation. The contract does not guarantee termination; the supplied input does not define width or the detailed root representation.

cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qt_nil.description: The lemma states that, assuming the implicit cjrGS(Σ) and invGS_gen(HasLc, Σ) instances, qt_nil satisfies a partial-correctness WP contract: if it returns a value v, then v represents an empty point list, meaning there is an object o with v = ov o and ownership of its fields containing false, 0, 0, and unit. The program invokes a function whose body uses New with those values; the input does not establish New’s precise runtime or layout semantics. The contract does not assert termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qt_power.description: For any natural number d, under the supplied cjrGS and invGS_gen typeclass assumptions, this lemma states that calling qt_power with the integer representation of d satisfies a partial-correctness contract: if the call returns, its result is the integer value 2^d, as defined by width d. No additional resource premise is stated, and the contract does not guarantee termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qt_power_v.description: For any natural number d, this lemma states a partial-correctness WP contract: applying the recursive qt_power function to a structure containing the integer encoding of d returns, if it terminates, the integer value 2^d. Its body returns 1 when d ≤ 0 and otherwise recursively computes the result for d − 1 and doubles it. The contract assumes the displayed CJR and invariant typeclass context and gives no additional explicit precondition; it does not assert termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.helpers.wp_qt_seed.description: The lemma states that, given ownership of an empty quadtree node n represented by node_rep at depth d and rectangle b, calling qt_seed with n and the two integer coordinates of p is safe and, if it returns, yields the unit value and ownership of the same node representing Leaf p, with d and b unchanged. This is a partial-correctness contract: it does not guarantee termination. No premise requires p to lie within b.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion.wp_insert_d.description: The lemma states that, if point p already belongs to tree t and tree_rep d t v supplies ownership of its representation at v, inserting p’s coordinates returns Boolean false and restores the same representation whenever the call terminates. The representation includes d ≤ 30, validity of t within domain d, and ownership of the tree’s fields and nodes. This is a partial-correctness WP contract: it preserves the represented tree but does not guarantee termination or establish that every memory location remains unchanged.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion.wp_insert_e.description: The lemma states that, if point p lies within rectangle b (including its lower boundaries and excluding its upper boundaries) and the required ownership describes an empty quadtree node at object o, calling insert_self with that object, depth d, and p’s coordinates satisfies a partial-correctness contract: if it returns, the same object represents some tree t' satisfying valid d b t', its contents are p added to the original empty tree’s contents, and the returned Boolean indicates whether p was previously absent. The supplied input does not define valid or contents, so their precise meanings cannot be expanded further. This WP contract does not guarantee termination.

The lemma states that if b is a square with side length width d, t is a valid quadtree within b at depth d, and p already belongs to t, then owning the node representation of t at n supports calling insert_self with n, d, and p’s coordinates: if the call returns, it returns false and restores ownership of a representation of the same tree t at n. This is a partial-correctness WP contract; it does not guarantee termination or establish that every memory field remains untouched.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion.wp_insert_l.description: This lemma states a partial-correctness contract for inserting point p into an object representing a leaf containing q at depth d+1. It assumes b is a square of side width(d+1), both points lie within b (including its lower boundaries but excluding its upper boundaries), and insertion already satisfies the corresponding contract for every valid depth-d child subtree whose box contains p. Given ownership of the leaf’s representation, the call is safe and, if it returns, leaves the same object representing a valid tree with contents equal to the old contents union {p}, returning true exactly when p was previously absent. The WP contract does not guarantee termination; the supplied input does not define width or contents further.

The lemma states that if b is a square of side length width 0, both p and q lie within its lower-inclusive, upper-exclusive bounds, and object o is owned as a representation of Leaf q at depth zero, then calling insert_self with o, depth zero, and p’s coordinates satisfies a partial-correctness contract. If the call returns, o represents some tree t′ satisfying valid 0 b, its contents are the old contents union {p}, and the returned Boolean indicates whether p was absent from the old contents. The supplied unit_unique lemma implies p = q under these premises. The definition of valid is not supplied, so its additional requirements are unspecified here. The WP contract does not guarantee termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion.wp_insert_r.description: This lemma states that if point p lies outside the square domain from (0,0), inclusive, to (width d,width d), exclusive, and v satisfies tree_rep d t v, then inserting p through qt_insert is partially correct: if the call returns, it returns the Boolean false and restores the same tree_rep d t v assertion. The representation premise includes d ≤ 30, validity of t for that domain, and ownership of the object fields and represented nodes. This contract does not guarantee termination; the supplied definitions do not further explain width or validity.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion.wp_qt_inser.description: Assuming ownership of a representation of tree t at value v, which includes d ≤ 30 and validity within domain d, this theorem gives a partial-correctness contract for inserting point p: if the call returns, v represents a valid tree t′ whose points are the original points plus p when p lies inside the domain, and otherwise are unchanged. It returns true exactly when p is inside the domain and was not already present; returning false also guarantees t′ = t. The domain includes its lower boundaries and excludes its upper boundaries. This contract does not guarantee termination.

This theorem states a partial-correctness contract for inserting point p into a quadtree: assuming b is a square of side width d, t is valid at depth d within b, p lies inside b (including its lower boundaries and excluding its upper boundaries), and node_rep supplies ownership of t’s representation at n, calling insert_self with n, d, and p’s coordinates is safe and, if it returns, preserves ownership at n of a valid tree whose contents are the old contents plus p. Its result encodes true exactly when p was previously absent, and false otherwise. The WP contract does not guarantee termination; the supplied input does not define width or the concrete runtime layout.

This theorem states a partial-correctness contract for inserting point p into a quadtree: given ownership of tree_rep d t v, which includes d ≤ 30 and validity of t in its domain, if qt_insert terminates, the same value v represents some valid tree t′ whose contents add p when p lies inside the domain and otherwise remain unchanged. The returned Boolean is true exactly when p is inside the domain and was not already present. The domain includes its lower coordinate bounds and excludes its upper bounds. The contract preserves the representation resources but does not guarantee termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion_helpers.bra.description: branch_call constructs a specialized version of the quadtree insertion branch by substituting n for "node", the integer encoding of d + 1 for "d", the integer encodings of p’s two coordinates for "x" and "y", and the recursive closure insert_self for "qt_insert_node". The branch loads the node’s midpoint and four children, selects a child using the coordinates, and makes a recursive insertion call with depth decreased by one, so the supplied depth becomes d. This is a definition of an expression, with no stated correctness contract or termination guarantee; the exact child-selection rule and recursive insertion behavior are not supplied.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion_helpers.ins.description: insert_post defines an Iris postcondition asserting that some quadtree t' is valid at depth d within rectangle b, contains exactly the old tree t's points together with p, and is represented in memory by node n with the ownership described by node_rep. The value v is the Boolean literal true exactly when p was absent from t, and false otherwise. Validity requires leaves to lie in their assigned rectangles and branches to respect the depth bound. This definition supplies no preconditions or proof that insertion satisfies it; used in a partial-correctness WP contract, it describes the result if execution returns, without guaranteeing termination.

insert_self defines a recursive closure named qt_insert_node, with argument binder args and body qt_insert_node_body. The body unpacks node, d, x, and y, then reads the node’s tag: tag 0 calls qt_seed and returns true; tag 1 loads the stored point and returns false if it matches (x, y), otherwise running qt_split; other tags run qt_insert_branch. The supplied input does not establish the precise behavior of those helpers, memory-layout requirements, correctness, or termination.

install_call builds a program that sequentially writes integer 2 to field 0 of n, integer 0 to fields 1 and 2, xmin(b) + width(d) and ymin(b) + width(d) to fields 7 and 8, and a, c, e, f to fields 9–12, then runs branch_call n d p. That branch expression substitutes n, depth d + 1, the two coordinates of p, and insert_self into qt_insert_branch. The input does not establish the meanings of these fields or the memory conditions needed for the stores, and this definition supplies no correctness contract or termination guarantee.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion_helpers.wp_.description: The lemma states a partial-correctness contract for inserting point p into a quadtree branch at depth d+1: assuming its box is a square of the prescribed size, the branch is valid, p lies inside the box, and recursive insertion satisfies the corresponding contract for every valid child containing p, ownership of the branch’s memory representation supports running branch_call. If the call returns, the same root represents a valid tree whose contents are the original contents plus p, and the returned Boolean is true exactly when p was previously absent. This WP contract does not guarantee termination.

The lemma states a partial-correctness contract for installing four child nodes into object o and then inserting point p. It assumes b is a square of depth d+1, the four subtrees form a valid branch, p lies within b, recursive insertion satisfies the stated contract for any valid child containing p, and ownership is available for o’s initial leaf-shaped fields and all four child representations. If install_call returns, o represents a valid tree whose contents are the original branch’s contents plus p, and the returned Boolean is true exactly when p was previously absent. The WP contracts do not guarantee termination.

The lemma states that, given ownership of an empty node n represented by node_rep at depth d and rectangle b, calling qt_seed with n and the two integer coordinates of p has a partial-correctness WP contract: if it terminates, it returns unit and provides ownership of the same node representing Leaf p, with d and b unchanged. The supplied body specifies stores of tag 1 and the coordinates into fields 0, 1, and 2. No premise requires p to lie within b, and the contract does not guarantee termination.

The lemma states a partial-correctness contract for splitting a quadtree leaf containing q and inserting p. It assumes b is a square of size width(d+1), both points lie inside b, the object o’s leaf fields are owned, and recursive insertion satisfies the stated contract for every valid child tree whose box contains p. The split creates four children, places q in its chosen child, and proceeds with insertion. If execution returns, o represents a valid tree containing exactly the old leaf’s contents together with p, and the returned Boolean indicates whether p was absent before insertion. This WP contract does not guarantee termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.insertion_model.seede.description: The definition seeded takes a quadrant k and a point p (a pair of integers) and constructs a quadtree branch with Leaf p in the child position selected by k—LL, LR, UL, or UR—and Empty in the other three positions. It imposes no condition on the point’s coordinates and does not establish that the point geometrically belongs to the selected quadrant.

The lemma states that for any quadrant k and point p, the contents of seeded k p are exactly the singleton set containing p. The definition of seeded places a leaf containing p in the child selected by k and leaves the other three children empty; contents combines the contents of all children by union. No additional premises are stated.

The lemma states that if point p lies in the child rectangle for quadrant k of rectangle b, computed using d, then the tree seeded k p is valid for b at depth d + 1. This tree has one branch containing a leaf with p in quadrant k and empty trees in the other three quadrants. Validity requires that leaf to lie in its corresponding child rectangle, while empty trees are always valid. Rectangle membership includes the lower bounds and excludes the upper bounds.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.bv.description: The definition bv takes a Boolean b and represents it as a literal value by wrapping it first with LitBool and then with LitV. It has no stated premises.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.fields.description: The definition fields takes an integer object identifier o and a list of values vs and produces an Iris proposition asserting ownership of each field of ObjId o: the field at each list index i contains the corresponding value v. These assertions are combined using separating conjunction, so their ownership resources must be held separately. The definition assumes a cjrGS(Σ) instance; the input does not give the precise semantics of field ownership or assert anything about fields outside the list.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.fields_look.description: The lemma says that if looking up index i in vs yields v, then ownership of all the listed fields of object o can be split into ownership of field i with value v and a resource that restores ownership of all those fields when that field ownership is returned. Here, fields o vs means separate ownership of each indexed field listed in vs, under the implicit cjrGS(Σ) context.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.fields_upda.description: If the list vs contains v at index i, this lemma says that ownership of all fields of object o described by vs can be split into ownership of field i with value v and a resource that rebuilds ownership of all fields when given ownership of field i with any value w, updating vs at i to w. Here fields combines ownership of each listed field using separating conjunction; the lemma describes how ownership resources can be taken apart and reassembled, rather than asserting that a program performs an update.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.is_quadtree.description: is_quadtree d S v is a separation-logic assertion saying that some abstract quadtree t contains exactly the set of points S and is represented by v at depth d. Its representation requires d ≤ 30, validity of t for domain d, and ownership of an object with fields storing d, width d, and a root satisfying node_rep. Contents are empty for an empty tree, a singleton for a leaf, and the union of the four children’s contents for a branch. The supplied input does not define the precise validity or node-representation conditions; this is an assertion, not a WP contract or a termination claim.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.iv.description: The definition iv takes an integer z of type Z and wraps it as an integer literal value, LitV (LitInt z). It has no stated premises; the supplied input does not establish any further properties.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.node_rep.description: node_rep defines a separation-logic ownership assertion relating a value n to a quadtree t with rectangle b and depth bound d. Each node is an object whose fields store the rectangle and a tag: 0 for empty, 1 for a leaf storing point p, or 2 for a branch. Empty nodes and leaves use zero split coordinates and unit child values. A branch requires positive depth, stores split coordinates and four child values, and separately owns the four corresponding subtree representations at depth d−1 in their child rectangles. The definition recurses structurally on t; it imposes no explicit requirement that leaf points lie inside their rectangles, and the supplied input does not define width. This is an ownership assertion, not a WP contract or a claim about program correctness or termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.node_rep_ob.description: This lemma states that owning the representation node_rep d b t v entails the pure fact that v = ov o for some integer o, meaning v is an object-literal value. Every possible representation case explicitly includes this equality; a branch at depth zero is impossible because its representation is False. The premise includes ownership of the node’s fields and, for branches, its children’s representations, while the conclusion records only the object-value equality.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.node_values.description: node_values constructs a 13-element list containing, in order, the tag, the point’s two integer coordinates, the rectangle’s xmin, ymin, xmax, and ymax fields, mx and my, and the four supplied values ll, lr, ul, and ur. The first nine entries are wrapped as integer literal values using iv; the last four are included unchanged. This definition imposes no conditions on these inputs, and the supplied source does not establish what the tag, mx, my, or final four values represent.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.ov.description: The definition ov takes an integer o of type Z and constructs LitV (LitObj o), wrapping o first with LitObj and then with LitV. The supplied input does not establish what these constructors represent or what runtime or layout metadata they require.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.point_list.description: point_list xs v is a recursive separation-logic assertion describing ownership of a linked representation of a list of integer-coordinate points, with v referring to its first object. An empty list owns an object whose four fields contain false, zero, zero, and unit. A nonempty list beginning with (x,y) owns an object with fields true, x, y, and a tail value, together with separate ownership satisfying point_list for the remaining points at that tail. This defines an ownership predicate, not a WP contract or a claim about program correctness or termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.point_list_.description: The lemma states that ownership of point_list xs v entails the pure fact that v = ov o for some integer o, meaning v is an object literal. This holds for both empty and nonempty lists because each case of point_list explicitly includes that equality alongside field ownership; the nonempty case also includes ownership of the remaining list. It assumes the implicit cjrGS(Σ) context and makes no claim about program execution or termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.tree_domain.description: The lemma states that ownership of a quadtree represented by v at depth d with point set S entails the pure fact that every point in S lies within domain d, the rectangle Rect 0 0 (width d) (width d). Its premise means there exists a tree t whose contents are S and for which tree_rep d t v holds; the supplied input does not define tree_rep or specify whether rectangle boundaries are included. This is a logical ownership entailment, not a WP contract or a claim about program termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.tree_rep.description: tree_rep d t v describes ownership of an object representing quadtree t: d must be at most 30, and t must be valid in the square from (0,0) with width 2^d, with leaves inside their assigned rectangles and no branches at depth zero. The value v identifies an object whose three fields store d, that width, and a root value; separately owned node fields recursively represent empty nodes, leaves, or four children in their respective subrectangles. The precise node layout and rectangle boundary conventions are not supplied. This is an ownership assertion, not a WP contract or a claim about program termination.

cjr.quadtree.proof.ownership.uv.description: The definition uv names the unit literal value, written LitV LitUnit in the source and rendered as (). No premises or further properties are stated.

cjr.quadtree.proof.routing.child_tree.description: child_tree selects one of four values of the same type A according to the quadrant k: LL returns ll, LR returns lr, UL returns ul, and UR returns ur. The type A is implicit, and quadrant has exactly these four constructors. Despite its name, this definition does not require the values to be trees.

cjr.quadtree.proof.routing.overlap.description: The definition overlap says that two rectangles b and r overlap when each rectangle’s minimum x-coordinate is strictly below the other’s maximum x-coordinate, and the same holds for their y-coordinates. For rectangles with positive width and height, this means their interiors overlap; merely touching at an edge or corner does not qualify. The supplied rectangle record stores four integer coordinates but imposes no ordering on them, so the definition itself does not require valid, nondegenerate rectangles.

cjr.quadtree.proof.routing.overlap_dec.description: This declaration registers a global instance that decides whether rectangles b and r satisfy overlap: each rectangle’s minimum x-coordinate is strictly below the other’s maximum x-coordinate, and likewise for y. The strict inequalities exclude mere boundary touching. No proof or implementation is supplied here, so the input states the decision instance without showing how it is established.

cjr.quadtree.proof.routing.query_pruned.description: The lemma states that if b is a square with side length width d, t is valid at depth d within b, and b does not overlap the query rectangle r, then query_model r t returns the empty list. Validity requires leaves to lie in their assigned rectangles and branches to have positive remaining depth with valid children; the supplied valid_contents lemma places all stored points inside b. The query filters the tree’s enumerated points using inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Overlap uses strict inequalities in both dimensions, so rectangles that merely touch at an edge do not overlap.

cjr.quadtree.proof.routing.routed_member.description: The lemma states that, if b is a square of side length width(S d) and the branch with children ll, lr, ul, and ur is valid at depth S d within b, then any point p belongs to the whole branch’s contents exactly when it belongs to the child selected by route d b p. Validity requires each child to be valid in its corresponding quadrant at depth d, and routing selects a quadrant by comparing p’s coordinates with the horizontal and vertical split values, assigning equality to the right or upper side.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.all_bounds.description: all_bounds recursively defines a condition on a quadtree, a box, and a depth: each visited box must have ordered x and y limits between 0 and 1073741824 inclusive. A branch is forbidden at depth zero; at depth S h, all four subtrees must satisfy the condition at depth h in their respective child boxes, formed using midx and midy, whose definitions are not supplied. Empty nodes and leaves impose no further condition, so leaf points are not checked against their boxes. Recursion is structurally on the tree.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.box_bounds.description: box_bounds defines a condition on a rectangle b: its integer coordinates must satisfy 0 ≤ xmin ≤ xmax ≤ 1073741824 and 0 ≤ ymin ≤ ymax ≤ 1073741824. Thus both coordinate ranges are ordered and lie within these inclusive bounds; equal endpoints are allowed. This definition states the condition but does not prove that any particular rectangle satisfies it.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.child_bounds.description: The lemma states that if rectangle b has both side lengths equal to width(S d), where S d is the successor of d, and its x and y endpoints are ordered and lie between 0 and 1073741824 inclusive, then any quadrant child selected by k also has ordered endpoints within those limits. The child is formed by splitting b at midx d b and midy d b; the supplied midpoint_bounds lemma states that these split coordinates lie within b under the same premises.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.decrement_int64.description: The lemma states that for any natural number d less than 30, converting its successor to an integer and subtracting 1 gives exactly the integer conversion of d, and that this result lies within the signed 64-bit range, from −9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.domain_bounds.description: The lemma states that for any natural number d at most 30, domain d satisfies box_bounds: its x and y lower bounds are nonnegative and no greater than their respective upper bounds, which are at most 1,073,741,824. The domain is defined as Rect 0 0 (width d) (width d), and the supplied width lemmas state that width d is positive and, under the same premise, within that limit. The intended rectangle interpretation is suggested by this definition, though Rect and its coordinate accessors are not defined in the input.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.doubling_int64.description: The lemma states that for any natural number d less than 30, doubling width d, where width d = 2^d, gives an integer within the signed 64-bit range, from -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807 inclusive.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.int64.description: The definition int64 is a predicate on an integer z that holds exactly when z lies between −9223372036854775808 and 9223372036854775807, inclusive—the range of signed 64-bit integers. It expresses a numerical bound, rather than converting z to a machine integer.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.leaf_coordinate.description: The lemma states that if a rectangle b has ordered x and y bounds between 0 and 1,073,741,824, and point p lies inside it, including the lower edges but excluding the upper edges, then both coordinates of p lie within the signed 64-bit integer range, from −9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.midpoint_bounds.description: The lemma states that if b is a square with side length width(d+1), and its integer coordinates satisfy 0 ≤ xmin ≤ xmax ≤ 1073741824 and 0 ≤ ymin ≤ ymax ≤ 1073741824, then midx(d,b) and midy(d,b) lie within the corresponding inclusive coordinate bounds. These values are the lower coordinates plus width(d), which is half the square’s side length according to the supplied width_succ statement.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.midpoint_int64.description: The lemma states that for any natural number d and rectangle b, if b is a square with side length 2^(d+1) and its coordinates satisfy 0 ≤ xmin ≤ xmax ≤ 1073741824 and 0 ≤ ymin ≤ ymax ≤ 1073741824, then both midpoint coordinates, xmin + 2^d and ymin + 2^d, lie within the signed 64-bit integer range, from −9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807. This is a mathematical range claim; the supplied input contains no proof establishing it.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.power_result_in.description: The lemma states that for any natural number d at most 30, width(d), defined as 2 raised to the power d, lies within the signed 64-bit integer range from −9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807. The supplied related lemmas state that width(d) is positive and, under the same premise, at most 1073741824; no proof is supplied here.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.root_all_bounds.description: The lemma states that if the natural-number depth d is at most 30 and t satisfies valid d (domain d) t, then all_bounds d (domain d) t holds. Thus the root box and every recursively assigned child box have ordered coordinates satisfying 0 ≤ xmin ≤ xmax ≤ 1073741824 and 0 ≤ ymin ≤ ymax ≤ 1073741824. At each branch the depth decreases by one; branches at depth zero are excluded. This conclusion bounds the boxes; leaf membership follows from the separate validity premise.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.stored_bounds_i.description: The lemma states that if a rectangle b satisfies box_bounds—its coordinates obey 0 ≤ xmin ≤ xmax ≤ 1,073,741,824 and 0 ≤ ymin ≤ ymax ≤ 1,073,741,824—then all four coordinates lie within the signed 64-bit integer range, from −9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807. The supplied declaration states this implication but does not include its proof.

cjr.quadtree.spec.bounds.valid_all_bound.description: The lemma states that if b is a square with side length width d, its coordinate endpoints are ordered and lie between 0 and 1073741824, and t is valid at depth d in b, then those same coordinate bounds hold for every box recursively associated with t. Validity requires each leaf’s point to satisfy in_rect in its assigned box and each branch to have positive remaining depth, with valid children in the four child boxes. The supplied input does not define width, child_box, or in_rect, so their precise interpretations remain unspecified.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.admissible.description: The definition admissible d S states that every point in the set S lies within domain d, the rectangle from (0, 0) to (width d, width d): both coordinates must be at least zero and strictly less than width d. It places no condition on points outside S, and the empty set satisfies it automatically. The supplied input does not define width, so its relationship to d is unspecified.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.build_tree.description: build_tree constructs a quadtree from a natural-number depth, a rectangle, and a list of integer-coordinate points. An empty list gives Empty; a singleton gives a Leaf; and at depth zero, any nonempty list gives a Leaf containing only its first point. Otherwise, it creates four branches by filtering the full list for each child rectangle and recursively processing those points with depth reduced by one. This decreasing depth bounds recursion. No conditions on the rectangle or points are stated, and the missing definitions of midx, midy, and in_rect leave the precise subdivision and boundary behavior uncertain.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.build_tree_corre.description: The lemma states that if rectangle b has width and height width d and every point in xs lies within b (including its lower boundaries but excluding its upper boundaries), then build_tree d b xs produces a valid quadtree whose set of stored points is exactly the set of points in xs, ignoring duplicates and order. Validity means leaves lie within their assigned rectangles, branches occupy the four corresponding subrectangles, and no branch occurs at depth zero. The supplied input states this result but does not include its proof.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.child_box.description: child_box takes a natural number d, a rectangle b with integer coordinates, and a quadrant, and constructs the corresponding lower-left, lower-right, upper-left, or upper-right rectangle using b’s outer bounds and split coordinates xmin b + width d and ymin b + width d. ## Summary

Create a self-contained integer-point quadtree example under `quadtree/`, reusing the shared CJR/Iris framework and Gallina printer.

The final deliverable is **`quadtree/index.html`**: an offline HTML index linking individual rendered definitions and lemmas, extracted Cangjie files, the test report, and the benchmark report.

## Interface and algorithm

- `make(depth)` creates an empty tree covering `[0, 2^depth) × [0, 2^depth)`, requiring `0 ≤ depth ≤ 30`.
- `insert(tree, x, y)` returns `true` exactly when it adds a new in-bounds point. Duplicate or out-of-bounds insertion returns `false` and preserves the tree.
- `contains(tree, x, y)` returns exact membership; out-of-bounds coordinates return `false`.
- `range(tree, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)` returns a duplicate-free linked list of matching points. Rectangles are half-open; empty or reversed rectangles produce empty results. Result order is unspecified.
- Nodes are empty leaves, single-point leaves, or four-child branches. Quadrants are lower-left, lower-right, upper-left, upper-right; midpoint coordinates belong to upper/right halves.
- Splitting redistributes the existing point before inserting the new point. Distinct integer points separate before reaching unit cells.
- Store node bounds and branch midpoints. Calculate subdivision sizes using a verified doubling helper and existing CJR arithmetic.
- Range traversal prunes disjoint nodes and accumulates results without repeated concatenation.

## Specification and verification

Define a finite-set specification and executable Gallina reference model. For fixed domain \(D\), let \(I_p(S)\) insert an in-bounds point and \(Q_R(S)\) select points inside rectangle \(R\).

Prove:

- **Insertion commutativity:** \(I_p(I_q(S)) = I_q(I_p(S))\), including duplicate and rejected coordinates.
- **Insertion idempotence:** \(I_p(I_p(S)) = I_p(S)\).
- **Repeated-query idempotence:** repeated membership calls return the same Boolean; repeated range calls return equivalent duplicate-free lists while preserving the tree’s fields and structure.
- **Range distribution over union:** \(Q_R(S \cup T) = Q_R(S) \cup Q_R(T)\), for trees sharing a domain. Union is specification-level set union, with overlapping points included once.
- Subdivision coverage/disjointness, bounded depth, uniqueness, and exact operation semantics.

Equality in insertion laws concerns represented point sets. Query results are compared as sets or permutations; fresh allocations are allowed.

Define Iris ownership predicates for trees and result lists. Prove operation contracts and derive concrete operation-composition theorems validating the algebraic laws. Query contracts preserve the same structural tree model.

Use `Int64` coordinates and query endpoints, and prove stored-bound and midpoint calculations stay within its limits. Verification must pass `coqchk` and assumption auditing without admissions or new axioms.

## Directory layout and final HTML report

Keep example-specific specification, algorithm, proofs, extraction entry point, generated code, tests, benchmarks, results, and documentation under `quadtree/`. Provide local `build`, `verify`, `extract`, `test`, `benchmark`, `docs`, and `report` targets.

Root changes are limited to load paths, build/verification wiring, a README pointer, and required repository logs.

The report index contains:

- **Definitions and lemmas:** grouped by specification/model, algorithm, ownership predicates, correctness, and algebraic laws. Each entry links directly to its declaration anchor in a page generated by `rocq_readable`, with proofs omitted. Build this index from the renderer’s generated declaration navigation and stable anchors.
- **Extracted Cangjie:** list every generated `.cj` file, linking both the original file and an escaped HTML source view. Extract implementation code directly from verified CJR definitions.
- **Test report:** link an HTML report containing case results, randomized/algebraic validation summaries, compiler information, source hashes, and execution status.
- **Benchmark report:** link an HTML report containing workload descriptions, timing summaries, local charts, comparison methodology, machine/compiler metadata, and downloadable raw CSV/JSON results.
- **Verification summary:** show proof-checking and assumption-audit results, along with renderer errors or unsupported-syntax coverage.

Use relative links, local CSS and chart assets, escaped content, and no network dependencies. All report destinations remain inside `quadtree/`.

`make report` assembles the index after verification, extraction, documentation, tests, and benchmarks. Assembly fails if required artifacts are missing or recorded source hashes are stale. Keep generated HTML, extracted code, and report data in version control.

## Tests, benchmarks, and acceptance

Test empty trees, depth zero, domain boundaries, midpoint routing, duplicates, rejected coordinates, all quadrants, and deeply clustered points. Cover empty, reversed, disjoint, selective, overlapping, and whole-domain rectangles.

Validate algebraic laws on the unchanged extracted code:

- Insert point pairs in both orders and compare complete contents and membership.
- Repeat queries and check equivalent results and unchanged tree contents.
- Build trees representing \(S\), \(T\), and \(S \cup T\), then check range distribution with deduplicated result sets.
- Run seeded randomized operation sequences and insertion-order permutations against an independent flat-set oracle.

Compile and run using Cangjie 1.0.5, with configurable compiler and SDK paths.

Benchmark extracted CJR against an independent native Cangjie quadtree with identical semantics and subdivision policy, plus a flat collection using hash-indexed membership and range scanning. Use uniform, clustered, and deeply coincident-prefix datasets at 256, 4,096, and 16,384 unique points. Measure construction/insertion, membership hits/misses, and empty, selective, broad, and whole-domain queries.

Use two warmups, calibration toward 20 ms batches, seven trials across three processes, rotating implementation order, and allocation-aware repetition limits. Validate complete results outside timing and consume checked checksums inside measured batches. Save raw observations, medians/IQR, source hashes, compiler flags, machine metadata, and charts.

Acceptance requires completed functional and algebraic proofs, reproducible extraction, passing runtime tests, measured benchmarks, and a complete HTML index whose file links and declaration anchors all resolve. Visually inspect the index and representative linked pages at desktop and narrow widths.
